messages.subject: Error: Non-numeric Argument to Binary Operator
messages.subject_clean: Error: Non-numeric Argument to Binary Operator
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

I'm processing more Actigraph GT3X+ files with GGIR and I'm getting this error:

Error in FUN(x, aperm(array(STATS, dims[perm]), order(perm)), ...) :
  non-numeric argument to binary operator

I'm attaching the R console output for the file giving the error.

I hope you have some time to troubleshoot. Please let me know if there's anything I else you need.

Thanks so much for all your help!
~ Suni

Info:
Using GGIR version 1.2-2
GT3X+ hip data collected at 30 Hz from 12/17/2013 - 2/5/2014. I think the participant didn't return the device on time;)

P.S. If this error is due to the amount of days of data, could you let me know if there's a way to truncate the file? Thx!SVG

messages.subject: Limiting analysis to a timeframe, and changing how plots are drawn
messages.subject_clean: Limiting analysis to a timeframe, and changing how plots are drawn
messages.body_plain:
My colleagues and I are trying to run GGIR with GeneActiv Actiwatch Sleep data. We're all rather inexperienced with R (more used to Python, SPSS etc) but we're feeding GGIR the bin files, and we're getting some nice output.

The two main flies in the ointment at present are:

We can't figure out how to get the graphs in the 'file summary reports' folder to go from noon to noon. In the PLOS ONE paper, the graphs seem to do just that, which is ideas for sleep analysis. But we're getting midnight to midnight. We're new to this package and it's not obvious what argument to pass to GGIR to get it to behave this way.
We've tried using maxdur=7, or using start and end arguments with timestamps, but we still get output for the whole bin file. In a nutshell, our bin files fun from 2pm on a Monday for 14 days. We'd like output for week one, until 2pm on the second Monday, then a separate output for the second week, leading up to the third Monday. We realise we'll need to run the package twice, but at present we get an analysis of the whole data file regardless of the options we're playing with.

Here's what we're attempting (R v2.3.2 on OS X 10.11.3)...

g.shell.GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4),datadir=c("/Users/LHW/Analysis/sleeptestinput"),outputdir=c("/Users/LHW/Analysis/sleeptestoutput"),studyname=c(sleepstudy),f0=1,f1=2,do.report=c(2),overwrite=FALSE,visualreport=TRUE, M5L5res=5, use.temp=TRUE, printsummary=TRUE, print.filename=TRUE, maxdur=7)

Sorry if these are newbie questions. Any help anyone can offer will be hugely appreciated.

Lee

messages.body_plain:
1. Did you try using argument viewingwindow = 2?
2. You can look at the day by day summaries and split them by week yourself. Reports per week in a multi-week measurement are currently not supported by the package.
Vincent

messages.subject: winhr
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am using g.shell.GGIR and trying to get a few different values for winhr (window size in hours for L5 and M5 analysis. I would like to get values for M5 L5 for 1 or 2 hours periods (M1, M2) as well as 5 hours. Ideally I want to know the peak 1 hour of exercise each day.

In the documentation provided for g.analyse it has winhr = 5 (which is the default). Later on under g.shell it show winhr = c(5,10). To me this suggests that it is possible to set multiple values for winhr.

However my experience is that it takes only the first (I think) value provided to make the calculation and provides only a single set of values, always named M5hr_ENMO etc.

Is there a way to get multiple values of peak ENMO for different time periods short of running g.analyse multiple times for each value? Alternatively I am new to GGIR so I might have made an error in there.

Thanks for all your help. It is a great package.
Tad
